finding.title: Make AppUser/AuthState/AuthUser @freezed instead of hand-rolled classes without value equality
finding.why: AppUser, AuthState and AuthUser are plain hand-written classes (immutable, but no @freezed, no custom ==/hashCode), so two instances with identical field values compare unequal by reference identity — AuthState is literally the `state` type of a keepAlive Riverpod Notifier. Current consumers avoid the fallout by exclusively `.select()`-ing down to primitive sub-fields (e.g. `s.currentUser?.firebaseUid`, a String, in manage_tutors_providers.dart/app_shell.dart/persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart) rather than comparing whole AuthState values, so no concrete rebuild-storm is demonstrated today — but it is a landmine for the next `ref.watch(authStateProvider)` call that doesn't remember to add a `.select()`.
finding.recommendation: Convert to @freezed (or at minimum implement value ==/hashCode) — low-risk given the classes are small and already immutable.
acceptance_criteria: AuthState(...) == AuthState(...) is true for equal field values (documents the fix via a unit test)
build_runner regenerates cleanly with no call-site breakage

finding.title: Rename one of the two generated authStateProvider symbols to remove the name clash
finding.why: auth_providers.dart's codegen'd `authState()` function and auth_state_provider.dart's codegen'd `AuthStateNotifier` class both generate a top-level `authStateProvider` symbol of DIFFERENT types (Stream<AppUser?> vs AuthState notifier). The feature only works today because every internal call site remembers the workaround: the public barrel `hide`s one, and sign_in_controller.dart/account_picker_screen.dart import with an explicit prefix or hide clause. Any new file that imports auth_providers.dart directly without replicating that discipline gets the wrong authStateProvider (a compile-time type mismatch today, but still a maintenance trap that costs someone debugging time).
finding.recommendation: Rename the stream provider (e.g. firebaseAuthUserStreamProvider) so the collision — and the need for every future importer to remember the hide/prefix workaround — is removed entirely.
acceptance_criteria: Only one top-level authStateProvider symbol exists in the account feature
account.dart's barrel export no longer needs a hide clause for this symbol

finding.title: Stop leaking raw English InvalidInputException.reason to users; unify the diverged 6-vs-8 password-length rule
finding.rule: EH-5 (stable codes, never pre-formatted human messages) + Evans invariant-in-one-place

evidence.quote:
if (value.length < 6) {
    return 'Password must be at least 6 characters';

finding.why: InvalidInputException.reason is a hardcoded English string ('invalid format', 'must be at least 8 characters') and signup_screen.dart's `on InvalidInputException catch (e) { _showError(e.reason); }` (used by both _signUpCloud and _signUpLocal) renders it straight to the UI with no AppLocalizations pass — proven by this batch's own test asserting the literal English substring appears. For a bilingual EN/HE app, a Hebrew-locale user hitting this path sees untranslated English. The bug is latent today only because the sole live caller of LocalAuthService.signUp (_createOfflineAccount) always supplies a synthetic, always-valid UUID email/password — but the underlying invariant has already drifted: the form-level validator (auth_validators.validatePassword) accepts 6+ characters while LocalAuthService._minPasswordLength requires 8, so a form-valid 6-7 character password fed through any future real caller of LocalAuthService.signUp would throw this untranslated exception.
finding.recommendation: Give InvalidInputException (and siblings) a stable code/enum instead of a free-text reason, and have signup_screen.dart resolve it via AppLocalizations the same way _mapAuthError already does for Firebase codes; extract one shared minimum-password-length constant used by both auth_validators.dart and local_auth_service.dart.
acceptance_criteria: InvalidInputException exposes a typed code instead of (or alongside) a raw English reason string
signup_screen.dart resolves the code via AppLocalizations before showing it
auth_validators.dart and local_auth_service.dart reference one shared minimum-password-length constant
regression test: a 6-7 character password does not throw InvalidInputException through any LocalAuthService.signUp caller

finding.title: Add a tap-through test for SignupScreen's offline account-creation flow; expose LocalAuthService via a provider
finding.rule: TQ-8 (bug-prone paths need regression tests) + SM-7 (services constructed only via @riverpod provider)

evidence.quote: //   • Offline path — credential-less explicit "Create Offline Account"

finding.why: The file's own header claims 'Offline path' coverage, but every offline test only checks the button's text/visibility — none ever call tester.tap on it. Tapping it runs _createOfflineAccount -> _signUpLocal, which does a registry collision check, a SharedPreferences email reservation, a live DB-file swap via accountDbFileNameProvider, a real argon2id hash, a PendingLocalSignupStore.writePayload, and a recover() rollback invoked from three separate catch clauses. None of that orchestration is exercised. A regression in recover() (e.g. failing to release the reserved email or delete the orphan DB file) would permanently block future signups for that device/email or leave a stale DB-file pointer, and ship unnoticed. LocalAuthService has no @riverpod provider anywhere in the codebase (grep-confirmed only inline `LocalAuthService(dao: dao)` constructions in signup_screen.dart and twice in sign_in_controller.dart) so there is no seam to inject a fast fake PasswordHasher for a tap-through test — unlike sign_in_controller_routing_test.dart's Branches D/E, which hit the identical argon2id cost and transparently document and justify the skip with a `skip:` reason citing exact line numbers. This gap carries no such acknowledgment.
finding.recommendation: Add a provider (or accept an injectable PasswordHasher through the existing constructor param) so LocalAuthService can be faked in tests, then add a testWidgets case that taps 'Create Offline Account' and asserts the registry/DB/payload side effects plus a forced-failure case asserting recover() actually rolls back, following the tester.runAsync pattern already established in sign_in_controller_routing_test.dart.
acceptance_criteria: a testWidgets case taps 'Create Offline Account' and asserts a DeviceAccount row + PendingLocalSignupStore payload are written
a second case forces a failure mid-_signUpLocal and asserts recover() released the reserved email and deleted the orphan DB file
LocalAuthService is obtainable through a provider/injectable seam that tests can override with a fake PasswordHasher

finding.title: Extract the duplicated drift .sqlite-suffix delete helper out of AccountLifecycleService and PendingLocalSignupStore
finding.why: Both private _deleteDbFile methods encode the identical drift_flutter '.sqlite'-suffix-with-bare-name-fallback workaround, each discovered and fixed as a separate bug (each carries its own header comment and its own dedicated regression test in this batch: account_lifecycle_db_delete_test.dart and pending_local_signup_file_cleanup_test.dart). Any future drift_flutter version change to the on-disk filename scheme means this exact fix has to be found and reapplied in two places; missing one leaves orphaned .sqlite files on disk or a delete that silently no-ops.
finding.recommendation: Extract one shared deleteDriftDbFile(databasesPath, dbFileName) utility (e.g. under core/database/ or core/utils/) that both services call; keep both existing regression tests but retarget them at the shared utility.
acceptance_criteria: one shared function implements the .sqlite-suffix delete-with-fallback logic
AccountLifecycleService and PendingLocalSignupStore both delegate to it instead of each defining their own copy
both existing regression tests still pass
